title: Structures and Forces
summary: Types of structures (frame, shell and solid), the purposes of structures, static and dynamic loads, and the internal forces of tension, compression, bending, torsion and shear.

notes.text: An object made of parts joined together that can support a load (carry weight) without collapsing, while keeping its shape.

items: **Natural structures**: trees, birds' nests, spider webs, skeletons, termite mounds.
**Human-made structures**: bridges, towers, houses, chairs, cellphone masts.

rows: Frame structure
A skeleton of parts (members) joined together; the frame carries the load
Electricity pylons, roof trusses, bicycle frames, scaffolding, cranes
Shell structure
A thin outer covering that is hollow inside; the shape gives it strength
Eggs, crash helmets, cooldrink cans, car bodies, tortoise shells
Solid (mass) structure
Made of a large amount of solid material; strength comes from its weight
Dam walls, brick walls, pyramids, mountains

notes.label: Remember
notes.text: Many structures combine types. A car has a **frame** chassis and a **shell** body; a house has **solid** brick walls and a **frame** roof.

items: **Support**: hold up a load (a table, a bridge).
**Protect**: keep something safe (a helmet, a cellphone cover).

rows: Static load
A load that does not move or change
The weight of the bridge itself; a TV on a table
Dynamic load
A load that moves or changes
Cars driving over a bridge; wind blowing on a tower; people jumping on a trampoline

notes.text: When a load acts on a structure, forces develop inside its parts (members).

rows: **Tension**
Pulls or stretches a member
Cables of a suspension bridge, a rope in a tug-of-war
**Compression**
Pushes or squashes a member
Pillars holding up a roof, the legs of a chair
**Bending**
Tension on one side and compression on the other side of a beam
A plank across a stream with someone standing in the middle
**Torsion**
Twisting
Wringing a wet cloth, turning a screwdriver
**Shear**
Two forces in opposite directions that try to slide or cut parts past each other
Scissors cutting paper, a bolt holding two plates together

notes.caption: Tension pulls a member apart; compression pushes it together

notes.label: Exam tip
notes.text: Ropes, cables and chains can only resist **tension**. Pillars, columns and struts resist **compression**.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between a static load and a dynamic load?
questions.memo:
✓ A static load does not move or change, e.g. the weight of the structure (1)
✓ A dynamic load moves or changes, e.g. traffic or wind (1)

questions.prompt: Give THREE purposes of structures, with an example of each.
questions.memo: Any three (1 each, with example): support; protect; contain; span; shelter

questions.prompt: Explain why a car is a combination of structure types.
questions.memo:
✓ The chassis is a frame structure (1)
✓ The body is a thin shell structure (1)

questions.prompt: When a person stands in the middle of a plank across a stream, the plank bends. Which side is in tension and which in compression?
questions.memo:
✓ The top surface is in compression (1)
✓ The bottom surface is in tension (1)
